reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent; every finding re-verified against the live public repo and the published tags before fixing

records.finding: The README still deferred pkg.go.dev to a flip that had already happened — 'and pkg.go.dev once the repo is public' — in the very file this PR edits to retire such claims. It is also the README's only pkg.go.dev mention, so the checklist's new line about 'the README's pkg.go.dev locators' pointed at a private-era caveat rather than a locator.
records.reason: Replaced with an actual pkg.go.dev link.

records.finding: CONTRIBUTING's release-verification step asserted in the present tense that the module is private and that the checksum database therefore 404s — describing a state that no longer exists, and framing as blocked the exact step the checklist now records as executed. I wrote this line in PR #121 and did not revisit it.
records.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:212-215 vs a verified `go get` of core and adapter at v0.2.0 from an empty module with default GOPROXY/GOSUMDB.
records.reason: Rewritten; the proxy negative-cache caution it now carries is the real hazard that replaced the imagined one.

records.finding: The stated reason GitHub Pages stays off was a private-repo reason ('unavailable or publicly served for a private repo'), so neither branch of the disjunction applies now — and the new checklist prose cross-references this exact section as the authority for the policy.
records.reason: Rationale restated on grounds that survive the flip: two generated doc sites competing is how one goes stale. The policy is unchanged.

records.finding: The checklist is a state-of-record document and its new paragraph made a completeness claim that was wrong: it enumerated where the private claims lived and omitted CONTRIBUTING, which still carried two. A reader auditing the flip against this record would conclude the sweep was finished. The same paragraph scolds an earlier revision for exactly this undercount.
records.evidence: The paragraph's enumeration vs CONTRIBUTING.md:213 and :374 still live at the time.
records.reason: Enumeration corrected, and the paragraph now records the method failure — one phrasing grepped instead of the concept — so the next sweep reads the lesson.

records.finding: graph.yaml declared a founder boundary the flip retired: 'repo stays private until the pilot exit criterion'. Tracked config, not historical evidence, and it is the file stating the authorities under which this review runs.
records.evidence: graph.yaml:42; sibling boundaries on 40-41 remain accurate.
records.reason: Reworded to keep the authority it asserts (visibility is the founder's) and drop the spent condition. graph validate PASS.

records.finding: The new CLI acquisition step hard-codes v0.2.0 into a download URL and filename, and nothing updates or checks them at the next release. goreleaser puts the version in the asset name so GitHub's releases/latest/download alias cannot absorb it, the stale URL keeps returning 200, and test/docsnippets ignores sh fences.
records.evidence: docs/quickstart.md:65-67; .goreleaser.yaml name_template includes {{ .Version }}; no hits for 'releases/download' under test/, scripts/ or .github/workflows/.
records.reason: Not currently false, so left in place; CONTRIBUTING's release procedure gains an explicit step to bump it, which is where a releaser will actually look.
